A rising edge past 1V sends the step back to the first one

Sets all nine step weights to fresh random values between 0 and 1

Picks one of the four modes at random
A rising edge past 1V picks one of the four modes at random

Note — the lamp beside each output lights while that step is the one selected, or shows the crossfade level while fading is switched on.

Note — Select Chance weights a random draw and Skip Chance steps on then rolls against the new step's weight.
Note — Repeat Weight counts down from a step's weight before moving on, and Fixed Pattern adds each weight to a running total for its step and picks whichever total is highest.
Menu — Hold last value — makes an output hold the last voltage it carried instead of dropping to 0V when the step moves on
Menu — Fade while switching — crossfades between the old step and the new one instead of switching at once
Menu — Fade Time — sets how long that crossfade takes

switch18.notes: The panel prints Clock over the jack that configInput calls Trigger, and M-Rnd, S-Rnd and S-Inv over the randomize-mode, randomize-steps and invert jacks; the Signal input and the Mode switch carry no lettering at all. compute_weights at src/switch18.cpp:141 zeroes the weight of any step whose output jack is unpatched, which is what makes an unconnected output unreachable. A weight CV replaces the knob's value and is then multiplied by it, so the knob works as an attenuator once a cable is present rather than adding to the CV. The invert behaviour is an exclusive-or of the invert switch and the invert jack's gate level (src/switch18.cpp:171), so either one alone inverts and both together cancel; the switch's two choice names, Invert on Low and Invert on High, are ambiguous about which of the two they describe and are not quoted for that reason. All nine weight CV jacks carry the maker's second line 'Expects a 0-10V signal' and nothing more.

lines: Four rise-and-fall function generators with shapeable curves, plus a cascade section that plays them one after another, and a wall of outputs comparing and combining the four
Sets how long that channel takes to rise, 0.01 to 5 seconds before the speed switch multiplies it
Sets how long that channel takes to fall, 0.01 to 5 seconds before the speed switch multiplies it
Bends that channel's rise from logarithmic through linear at the centre to exponential
Bends that channel's fall from logarithmic through linear at the centre to exponential
Multiplies that channel's rise and fall times by five for slow, one for normal or a fifth for fast
Makes that channel run its rise and fall over and over instead of stopping after one pass; flicking it also starts a fresh pass
A rising edge past 1V starts that channel's rise and fall from the beginning
Multiplies that channel's rise time by its own voltage over ten, holding the result between 0.01 and 5 seconds, so the knob becomes an attenuator while a cable is here
Multiplies that channel's fall time by its own voltage over ten, holding the result between 0.01 and 5 seconds, so the knob becomes an attenuator while a cable is here
That channel's function, at the range its own menu entry sets, either from zero up or swinging either side of zero
10V while that channel is rising and 0V otherwise
10V while that channel is falling and 0V otherwise
Chooses the order the cascade plays the four channels in: A, B, C, D in turn, or all four in a fresh random order each pass, or one at a time at random with repeats allowed
Starts all four channels and the cascade from the beginning of their cycles
A rising edge past 1V starts all four channels and the cascade from the beginning of their cycles
A rising edge past 1V starts the cascade again from the beginning of its cycle, leaving the four channels where they are
Makes the cascade start a new pass as soon as it finishes one instead of stopping; flicking it also starts a fresh pass
Multiplies the cascade's rise and fall times by five for slow, one for normal or a fifth for fast, using the times of whichever channel it is playing
The cascade's function, one channel's rise and fall at a time, at the range its own menu entry sets
10V while the cascade is rising and 0V otherwise
10V while the cascade is falling and 0V otherwise
The lowest of the four channel functions, each scaled by its own range
The highest of the four channel functions, each scaled by its own range
The four channel functions added together and divided by four, each scaled by its own range
The two highest of the four functions averaged, on a fixed 0V to 10V scale whatever the channel ranges are
The two lowest of the four functions averaged, on a fixed 0V to 10V scale whatever the channel ranges are
10V while the first of the two channels named on it is above the second, and 0V otherwise, comparing the raw functions before any range is applied
The distance between the two channels named on it, subtracted from the range that pair is set to, so it is largest when the two are together
The distance between the two channels named on it, so it is zero when the two are together and largest when they are furthest apart
Note — the four channels come up with Loop switched on and a one second rise and fall, so the module runs as soon as it is added to a patch.
Note — a cable in a rise or fall CV jack multiplies the knob rather than adding to it, so 0V there stops that stage at its shortest and 10V leaves the knob alone.
Note — each channel, each pair section and the cascade has its own output range on the right-click menu, chosen from 1V, 2V, 3V, 5V and 10V, each either unipolar or swinging both ways.
Note — the All Ranges submenu can override every one of those at once; switching the override off again puts back the settings each section had before.
Note — the cascade plays only one channel at a time and takes its rise and fall times from that channel, so the cascade output is not a copy of any channel output.
Note — the four lamps in the middle show which channel the cascade is playing and how far through it is.
Note — this module is monophonic: every jack reads or writes one channel only.
Menu — All Ranges: Override individual range settings, +/- 1v, +/- 2v, +/- 3v, +/- 5v, +/- 10v, Unipolar — one output range for every section, applied while the override item is ticked
Menu — Channel A Range: +/- 1v, +/- 2v, +/- 3v, +/- 5v, +/- 10v, Unipolar — sets the output range of channel A
Menu — Channel B Range: +/- 1v, +/- 2v, +/- 3v, +/- 5v, +/- 10v, Unipolar — sets the output range of channel B
Menu — Channel C Range: +/- 1v, +/- 2v, +/- 3v, +/- 5v, +/- 10v, Unipolar — sets the output range of channel C
Menu — Channel D Range: +/- 1v, +/- 2v, +/- 3v, +/- 5v, +/- 10v, Unipolar — sets the output range of channel D
Menu — A <-> B Range: +/- 1v, +/- 2v, +/- 3v, +/- 5v, +/- 10v, Unipolar — sets the output range of the section between channels A and B
Menu — B <-> C Range: +/- 1v, +/- 2v, +/- 3v, +/- 5v, +/- 10v, Unipolar — sets the output range of the section between channels B and C
Menu — C <-> D Range: +/- 1v, +/- 2v, +/- 3v, +/- 5v, +/- 10v, Unipolar — sets the output range of the section between channels C and D
Menu — D <-> A Range: +/- 1v, +/- 2v, +/- 3v, +/- 5v, +/- 10v, Unipolar — sets the output range of the section between channels D and A
Menu — Cascade Range: +/- 1v, +/- 2v, +/- 3v, +/- 5v, +/- 10v, Unipolar — sets the output range of the cascade section

funcgen.notes: Six parameters are declared and never given a widget: PUSH_PARAM for each of the four channels (indices 12 to 15), CASCADE_TRIGGER_PARAM (18) and an unnamed ENV_FUNC_PARAM (19). The push parameters are read in process() at src/funcgen.cpp:324 but no button is added for them, so no click can reach any of the six and none carries a line or a tag. Eight outputs are likewise declared with no jack: A > C, C > A, B > D, D > B and the four A-C and B-D distance outputs (indices 9, 13, 14, 18, 21, 24, 27 and 30). Four of those eight — A > C, C > A, B > D and D > B — are never written by process() either; the panel only has sections between adjacent channels. CASCADE_LOOP_PARAM is marked TODO IMPLEMENT in the enum at src/funcgen.cpp:24 but is read at lines 348, 545 and 660 and does work. The panel prints almost nothing: Trig All, Min, Max and some waveform glyphs, so nearly every control is named only by its tooltip. Top 2 Average and Bottom 2 Average ignore the range settings and are always built on a 0 to 10V scale, unlike Minimum, Maximum and Average. All eight rise and fall CV jacks carry the maker's second line 'Expects a 0-10V signal' and nothing more.

supersaw.notes: The panel misspells the octave knob as Ocrtave; configParam calls it Octave. The panel letters the three waves A, B and C while configParam numbers them 1, 2 and 3, and the two middle-wave controls are lettered B-Wave and B-Width. Each oscillator's saw(), pulse() or triangle() advances the phase as a side effect (src/oscillator.hpp:32 to 38) and process() calls it twice per sample for each oscillator, once into the mix and once into that wave's own output (src/supersaw.cpp:262 and 263), so the phase advances two steps per sample and the wave outputs are one step ahead of what the mix uses. FREQ_C3 is 130.81 (src/oscillator.hpp:3), so the doubled advance puts 0V at the pitch input at about 261.6Hz. In the branch taken when the gate jack is unpatched, src/supersaw.cpp:292 applies the final level CV a second time to a value that already carries it (src/supersaw.cpp:248). Noise duration is 0 to 0.001 seconds and noise mix is 0 to 0.5. Eleven CV jacks carry the maker's second line 'Expects a 0-10V signal' and nothing more.

lines: Routes nine inputs to nine outputs, rearranging the routing on each clock by a rule the mode and entropy switches pick out of eighteen
Switches between treating the nine lines one at a time and treating them as pairs, so that each pair is moved together
Picks one of six families of rearrangement: Basic, Up, Down, Broadcast, Pairs and Triplets
Picks how far each clock moves the routing from where it is: Negative pulls it back towards straight through, Low makes a small change, and High makes a large one
A rising edge past 1V rearranges the routing by the rule the mode and entropy switches name
A rising edge past 1V puts the routing back to straight through, each input to the output of the same number
One of the nine signals to be routed; where it comes out depends on the routing as it stands
Carries whichever input the routing currently sends here, or a crossfade between the old and new ones while fading is switched on
Replaces the mode switch, a voltage of 0V to 10V picking one of the six in order; with trigger mode on, a rising edge steps or jumps to another mode instead
Replaces the entropy switch, a voltage of 0V to 10V picking one of the three in order; with trigger mode on, a rising edge steps or jumps to another setting instead
Replaces the channels switch, below 5V for one line at a time and 5V or above for pairs; with trigger mode on, a rising edge flips it instead
A rising edge past 1V rearranges the routing by the negative rule of the current mode, whatever the entropy switch is set to
A rising edge past 1V rearranges the routing by the low rule of the current mode, whatever the entropy switch is set to
A rising edge past 1V rearranges the routing by the high rule of the current mode, whatever the entropy switch is set to
Note — nothing happens until a clock arrives: the routing starts straight through and only a clock, or one of the three entropy clocks, changes it.
Note — the eighteen rules are the six modes crossed with the three entropy settings: Basic gives Unwind, Swap and Randomize, and Up and Down give Sort, Shunt and Rotate in that direction.
Note — Broadcast gives Split, Double and Blast, which set two or all nine outputs to the same input; Pairs and Triplets repeat the Basic rules in sets of two and three.
Note — the three entropy clock inputs act alongside the main clock, so one patch can pull the routing about with one clock and settle it with another.
Note — every output carries as many channels as the widest cable patched into any input.

Menu — Trigger mode: Enabled, Random mode — turns the three CV jacks into trigger inputs that step through their settings, and Random mode inside it makes each trigger jump to a random setting instead
Menu — Hold last value — makes an output hold the last voltage it carried when the input the routing sends it is unpatched, instead of dropping to 0V
Menu — Fade while switching — crossfades between the old routing and the new one instead of switching at once
Menu — Fade Time — sets how long that crossfade takes

randrouter.notes: The panel prints Clock, Reset, Entropy, High-E, Low-E, Neg-E, Mode and Chan; the nine signal jacks on each side carry no lettering. The three CV jacks each carry the maker's second line 'Expects a 0-10V signal'. The mode CV maps 0V to 10V onto the six modes by multiplying by 0.6 and rounding (src/randrouter.cpp:535), and the entropy CV onto the three settings by multiplying by 0.3 (src/randrouter.cpp:542); the channels CV is a plain threshold at 5V (src/randrouter.cpp:528). With trigger mode enabled those same three jacks are read as triggers instead. No family is written for the nine signal inputs or the nine outputs: the module routes whatever it is given and gives the voltage no meaning of its own. The eighteen rule names in the lines are the maker's, from the table in README.md.
